gadgets.versions: PHP 7.0.x (measured on 7.0.33 with the distro curl on Debian stretch)
gadgets.sink: host-allowlist bypass when the validated string and the fetched string are not the same string
gadgets.payload: url=0://127.0.0.1:80;<allowed-host>:80/   -> parse_url()['host'] is the whole '127.0.0.1:80;<allowed-host>:80' and satisfies a /<allowed-host>$/ suffix test, while curl re-parses that string and stops the host at 127.0.0.1:80
gadgets.effect: full SSRF to loopback through a host allowlist, with a clean Host header so the target vhost answers normally
gadgets.precondition: the code validates parse_url($url)['host'] and then passes that host (or any re-derived string) to CURLOPT_URL instead of the original URL; the allowlist regex has no left anchor or delimiter
gadgets.trap: filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_URL) is STRICTER for http:// than for an unknown scheme -- percent-encoded and bracketed hosts rejected under http:// are accepted under 0://, so retry a rejected host shape with a junk scheme before discarding it. Also: parse_url splits the port into its own key, so a :port in the submitted URL never reaches curl when only ['host'] is forwarded -- a port sweep that returns identical results is measuring nothing.

gadgets.sink: not a gadget here -- a measured DEAD END worth not re-testing
gadgets.effect: the first passes both gates and connects, but every port times out with 0 bytes because curl takes the bracketed v4-mapped IPv6 literal and nothing answers it in this container; the second does reach loopback but Apache replies 400 Bad Request because the Host header becomes '[127.0.0.1].<allowed-host>'. Both look like a working SSRF and neither delivers a usable response.
gadgets.trap: a connect that times out on EVERY port is not a firewall -- it is usually the wrong address family
